Recipe: {"endpoint": "/v1/completions", "ignore_eos": true, "logprobs": 5, "n": 1, "percentile_method": "nearest-rank, no interpolation", "return_token_ids": true, "seed": 20261021, "stream": true, "stream_options": {"include_usage": true}, "temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0}

How to read these rows honestly:

- TTFT is MEASURED-CLIENT and includes HTTP connect, queueing and prefill, so a load spike (see a max of ~2 s in one sample) is contention, not a fixed cost.
- decode tok/s on the 9-token rows is measured over 8 token intervals, and speculative decoding (dspark, 5 draft tokens) delivers 1-3 tokens per stream chunk: the per-sample 'max tok/chunk' column is the stream granularity. The 64-token steady row is the lower-variance decode estimate; neither row is a single-stream baseline while load_conditions.verdict is UNDER-LOAD.
- greedy_deterministic_across_samples can be false on the random-token fixture even at temperature 0: the fixture has flat near-tie ranks (task32-root-cause.md), so batch composition changes under co-tenant load flip near-ties. That is exactly why D39 forbids a token-equality gate; every sample's token ids are recorded.

## Prompt self-consistency: random-token fixture vs natural language

The D41/D48 130-token fixture prompt is 130 RANDOM token ids (seed 7; task32-root-cause.md says so explicitly). On a random-token continuation a correct model assigns the actual next token a low logprob and a large rank, so the fixture row below is EXPECTED behaviour and is NOT evidence of degeneracy or of an unusable oracle. The natural-language rows are the measured test of whether the served checkpoint predicts its own text.

| row | prompt nature | positions | target logprob mean | median | target rank median | target rank p90 | target rank == 1 (top-1 rate) |
| :-- | :-- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| b69-fixture-130 | random-token fixture (EXPECTED low) | 129 | -15.4204 | -14.3189 | 73804 | 117251.0 | 0.0 |
| nl-capital | natural language | 4 | -4.9285 | -3.1618 | 7.5 | 2477.0 | 0.25 |
| nl-rust | natural language | 10 | -5.6791 | -2.8381 | 5.5 | 108.0 | 0.3 |
| nl-chat | natural language | 10 | -1.8186 | -0.9064 | 1.0 | 31.0 | 0.6 |

Natural-language self-consistency verdict: **NATURAL-LANGUAGE-SELF-PREDICTION-NORMAL**

A natural-language row with median target rank >= 10000 and top-1 rate < 0.10 means the served checkpoint does not reproduce its own text continuation. The random-token fixture row is excluded from this test by construction.

The fixture row is kept to show the difference; do not read it as a degeneracy claim. A 'UNUSABLE-AS-DISTRIBUTIONAL-ORACLE' verdict would need every natural-language row to show median target rank >= 10000 and top-1 rate < 0.10.
